title: The machine learning lifecycle
goals: Distinguish fitting a rule from applying a fixed rule
Trace a small learning lifecycle with separate data
Report test evidence with its limits

prerequisite.prompt: A fixed rule matches 3 labels out of 4 tested cases. What fraction is correct, and does that prove it works on all future cases?
prerequisite.answer: 3 of 4, or 75 percent, are correct in these cases. It does not prove correctness on future cases.

vocabulary: An input value used to make a prediction
An observed target value supplied for an example
Using examples to select or adjust a model
Examples reserved from fitting and model choices for evaluation

lesson.title: From a written rule to a fitted rule

blocks.text: In Grade 7 you programmed an activity chooser using a rule supplied by a person. This week you will choose a rule by comparing its predictions with labelled examples. This small supervised learning task makes the learning process visible: people define the task and possible rules; training data determines which candidate fits best.

Imagine fictional practice cards with a measured width x and a category label, 0 or 1. Width uses invented units. We want to predict the category of another card from its width. The labels are provided observations in this exercise, not values generated by our prediction code. These invented cards demonstrate a method; they provide no evidence about real objects or students.

Before fitting, set aside the final two cards. They are visible here so you can follow the complete example, but do not use them to choose a rule. Our candidates predict 1 when width is at least 2, 4 or 6, and 0 otherwise. Choose the candidate with the fewest training mistakes. If candidates tie, choose the smaller threshold; fix this rule before testing.

blocks.title: Python 3 code

blocks.text: int(True) is 1 and int(False) is 0. For threshold 2, the training predictions are 0, 1, 1, 1: the width 3 card is wrong. For threshold 4, they are 0, 0, 1, 1: none is wrong. For threshold 6, they are 0, 0, 0, 1: the width 5 card is wrong. The printed rows are 2 1, then 4 0, then 6 1. Select threshold 4 using this training evidence and record it. The loop reports errors; the learner makes and records the selection.

blocks.title: Keep fitting and testing separate
blocks.caption: Read down the stages. Test results may inform later development, but they must not silently change the rule being tested.

lesson.title: Freeze the rule and test it

blocks.text: Freeze means do not change the chosen threshold during this evaluation. With threshold 4, widths 2 and 6 receive predictions 0 and 1. Compare them with the held out labels: both match. Report 2 correct out of 2 held out cards. Training results and test results answer different questions: did the rule fit the examples used to select it, and how did that fixed rule perform on these separate examples?

blocks.label: Keep threshold 4 fixed. An additional card has width 4 and observed label 0. Predict its category, decide whether it is correct, and update the held out count from 2 of 2.

blocks.text: A learner sees the width 4 test error, changes the threshold to 5, and reports the same cards as a fresh final test. The test labels have now influenced the model. Keep the original 2 of 3 result for the original rule. Record the change as development, then reserve genuinely unused examples for a later evaluation. Do not delete the difficult card or rename reused cards as new evidence.

A lifecycle continues after fitting: define the intended use, prepare and separate data, fit, evaluate, review the limits, and monitor any approved use. Evaluation can send us back to development. That return needs an honest record and a new final evaluation; it does not erase the earlier error.

This threshold model learned only a choice among three candidate values. People supplied the feature, labels, candidate family and tie rule. Learning does not imply understanding, and perfect training performance does not guarantee good predictions. Two correct test cards are too few to establish reliable performance for a broader population. Even a larger score would depend on how examples were collected and what use was intended.

blocks.label: Your report says the fixed model matched 2 of 2 held out cards. Write one supported claim, one claim this does not support, and one sensible next step.

workbook.title: Identify the learning decision
workbook.prompt: For the worked cards, name the input, label, three candidate thresholds and the information allowed to select a threshold.
workbook.answer: The input is width x and the label is the observed category 0 or 1. Candidates are 2, 4 and 6. Selection uses mistakes on the four training cards only; held out labels must not guide it.

workbook.title: Trace one candidate
workbook.prompt: Use threshold 6 on the four training widths 1, 3, 5 and 7. Write all predictions, identify each error, and explain why threshold 4 is selected.
workbook.answer: Predictions are 0, 0, 0, 1. The width 5 card is wrong because its label is 1. Threshold 6 has one training mistake; threshold 4 has zero and is selected.

workbook.title: Repair the report
workbook.prompt: A learner fits on all six worked cards and then reports 6 of 6 as independent test performance. Explain what is wrong and what evidence is needed.
workbook.answer: All six cards influenced fitting, so none of those six provides an independent test. Report this as performance on fitting data. Freeze the rule and evaluate it on unused examples; do not claim a new split of the same reused cards repairs the earlier evaluation.

workbook.title: Fit and evaluate independently
workbook.prompt: New training cards are (width 2, label 0), (4, 0), (6, 1), (8, 1). Candidates are 3, 5 and 7. Predict 1 when width is at least the threshold. Count training mistakes, select the fewest with smaller threshold breaking ties, and record the choice before testing. Held out cards are (3, 0), (7, 1), (5, 0). Give each test prediction, the correct count and a limited conclusion.
workbook.answer: Training mistake counts for thresholds 3, 5 and 7 are 1, 0 and 1; select 5 before examining test results. Held out predictions are 0, 1, 1. The width 5 card is wrong, giving 2 correct out of 3. This supports the result on these three cards only, not universal reliability. Preserve threshold 5 for this evaluation.

workbook.title: Decide the next step
workbook.prompt: After W4, a team changes its threshold because of the test error. Can the same three cards be an untouched final test for the changed model? Explain how to proceed.
workbook.answer: No. Their labels have influenced the revision. Keep the first result, log the new threshold and use the old cases for development or regression checks. Use fresh reserved cases for an independent final evaluation.

teacher.background: Teach the first Grade 8 machine learning lesson as two 45-minute sessions. The central distinction is selection from labelled training examples versus evaluation of a fixed rule on separate examples. This is a deliberately small supervised classification exercise, not a deployed card recognition system. Students can complete it on paper; Python checks their trace. Do not add neural-network terminology or external accounts. The training loop reports candidate mistakes, and students explicitly select and record the winner.
materials: Printed lesson and workbook; six fictional worked cards
Paper to cover the held out rows until a threshold is recorded
Optional local Python 3 editor; no packages or personal data needed
Prepare a fresh retry card set from the assessment guidance
sessions: Retrieve the Grade 7 idea of testing a fixed rule. Ask the prerequisite question and require a denominator in the answer.
Define width, label and threshold. Read the card table. Cover the held out rows and agree the three candidate values and tie rule before fitting.
Trace every prediction for thresholds 2, 4 and 6. Use W1 and W2. Have students explain a wrong prediction rather than only counting errors. Optionally run the Python loop.
Record threshold 4, then uncover held out cards. Complete the guided additional width 4 case. Compare training and held out results with separate denominators.
Retrieve the sequence define, separate, fit, freeze and test. Ask which step may use training labels and which records test results.
Discuss the unfair evaluation and complete W3. Show why changing a model after seeing test labels changes the status of those examples.
Collect W4 independently. Have each learner record the training errors and threshold before revealing the test rows. Record whether support was needed.
Discuss W5 and the exit claim. Offer the fresh retry after support where needed. Preserve both the original result and later correction.
teacher.guidedAnswer: The prerequisite answer is 3 of 4, or 75 percent, for those four cases only. Guided case: width 4 produces 1 at threshold 4, but its label is 0, so it is wrong; the updated held out result is 2 of 3. Exit: a supported claim is that the fixed threshold matched both of these two cards. It does not show all future cards will be correct. A reasonable next step is to evaluate more unused examples chosen to represent the intended task, while recording the sampling limits.
misconceptions: The model wrote its own task
People chose the input, label meaning, candidate thresholds and selection rule. Learning here means choosing a parameter using the training examples.
Zero training mistakes means no future mistakes
Training performance measures the examples used to choose the threshold. The additional width 4 card shows how a fitted model can be wrong on a different example.
A better score makes reused test data independent
Once test labels influence a revision, the examples are part of development. Preserve the history and use unused cases for a later independent evaluation.
teacher.assessment: Require W4 training counts 1, 0, 1, selection 5, held out predictions 0, 1, 1 and result 2 of 3, plus an explanation of separation and limits. Assess the explanation before offering hints. Fresh retry: training (1,0), (5,0), (7,1), (9,1), candidates 4,6,8. Mistakes are 1,0,1; choose 6. Held out (2,0), (8,1), (6,0) produces 0,1,1 and 2 of 3. Ask why the final error must remain in the report. Correct arithmetic without keeping fitting and testing separate is not sufficient exit evidence.
teacher.support: Use a prediction grid with one row per card and one column per candidate. Cover held out rows until the choice is written. Read pairs aloud as width then label. Extension: candidates 4 and 5 both fit the worked training set with zero errors; the predeclared smaller-threshold tie rule chooses 4. Explain why the test labels must not break this tie.
teacher.next: Week 2 examines features, labels and which information exists at prediction time. Carry forward the recorded split, threshold and test result. Teacher reference for data separation and leakage: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html#data-leakage (reviewed 2026-09-26).
